hooks.note: Swift's weak delegate is Model itself; Kotlin's Model passes a ModelReplayEffectDelegate adapter that nothing else references, so a WeakReference is collected at the next GC and replayEffectStatus/replayEffectCompleted never arrive. A strong reference keeps the adapter (ReplayEffect is short-lived). Retire it once a re-translation follows E10.md's delegate rule (a plain strong property).
SettingsStreamReplayTransitionType.toString() is the localized display name, so any non-English locale fell through to None; rawValue is none/fade/stingers (Swift switch replay.transitionType).
Swift's replaced MediaPlayer runs deinit (stopOutputTimer) at once; MediaPlayer.close() is that deinit.
Swift's removed MediaPlayer runs deinit (stopOutputTimer) at once; MediaPlayer.close() is that deinit.

cameraPosition is the SettingsSceneCameraPosition enum, never a SettingsCameraId, so the is-check was always true and play, pause, next, previous and seek found no player (Swift: cameraPosition == .mediaPlayer).
Swift's timer closure captures [weak self], so a dropped player's deinit stops the timer; the Kotlin closure must not root the player.
